newsitem.title: GERMANY: Ex-E.German guards on trial for 1966 shooting.
newsitem.headline: Ex-E.German guards on trial for 1966 shooting.

text.p: Three former East German border guards went on trial on Monday accused of killing a drunken West Berliner they mistook for an East German trying to escape over the Berlin Wall more than 30 years ago.
Reinhard Jaensch, 52, Franz Heinl and Ulrich Fandrich, both 51, were jointly charged with shooting the 31-year-old man, who fell into a canal which ran alongside the Cold War frontier.
Prosecutors say the three fired 176 shots as the man tried to swim back to the bank and four of the shots killed him.

Jaensch, who was in charge of the border post at the time told the court he had not tried to kill the man but shot close to him to force him "back" towards the eastern bank, thinking he was trying to escape to the West.

Extreme secrecy shrouding East Germany's fortified borders has made it impossible to find out exactly how many people were shot dead or killed by landmines as they tried to flee west from the 1950s up to the fall of the Wall on November 9, 1989.

German justice authorities estimate about 800. Berlin courts have convicted 29 lower-ranking border guards of murder but given most of them suspended sentences because they were young recruits following orders.

The 1966 killing was the fifth border shooting incident to come to trial in which former West German citizens were killed. The vast majority of cases involved former East German citizens trying to escape to the capitalist West.
